reviewer_build: build/20-F025-rev (fresh configure + build of the committed head; wt/20-F025 git status clean, HEAD 99a0b10853d4)
reasons: llvm/lib/Target/RISCV/PULP/PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp:1009 and :1030 together with :1068 (new regression: the compiler crashes with a segfault). The fixed-point loop now handles a loop in one of two orders: pad first, expand later. The old code only did it the other way round (expand, then pad, in the same visit). When a tiny constant-count loop is padded first, its nops go into a new PadMBB made by MF.CreateMachineBasicBlock() with no IR BasicBlock (:1068). If a later iteration switches that loop to the long form, LoopStartMBB = *MBB.succ_begin() (:1009) is that PadMBB, and BlockAddress::get(LoopStartMBB->getBasicBlock()) (:1030) is called with nullptr and segfaults. Repro: logs/20-F025-review/crash/t.c, `clang --target=riscv32-unknown-elf -march=rv32imc_zfinx_xpulpv2 -mabi=ilp32 -O2 -mllvm -pulp-loop-range-immediate=0 -c t.c` (also =1,2,3, and rv32im). It crashes in 'PULP Hardware Loop Fixup' on @g (a one-store loop of 1000 iterations), in both build/20-F025 and build/20-F025-rev. int-20 compiles all of them. -pulp-loop-range-immediate=0 is the setting the stock fuzzer uses (benchmarks/hwloop-fuzz/one.sh), and the new cl::opt comment advertises it ('0 makes every lp.setupi use the long form'). The worker's stock-fuzzer run did not hit it only because fuzz loops have runtime counts (lp.setup, never lp.setupi). The default options are not affected: a loop that needs padding cannot later exceed 58 bytes. But the ordering hazard is real, and the note's termination argument (:883) does not cover it. Fix direction (worker's choice): make the expansion not depend on the pad block (e.g. take the loop start from the header block, not the first successor, or skip BlockAddress::get when the block has no IR block, as upstream code does for blocks without an IR block), or check the long-form decision before padding. Include a -pulp-loop-range-immediate=0 constant-count one-instruction loop in the proposed lit test.

notes/20/F025.md 'Why this is equivalent' / 'Alignment (2)' and result.json code_change (note: claims contradicted by measurement). (a) 'exact when the setup is 4-byte aligned' is wrong. getInstSizeInBytes gives 4 bytes for conditional branches, PseudoBR and PseudoRET with MBB operands, but the MC layer emits them compressed as c.beqz/c.bnez/c.j/c.jr (2 bytes). Branch relaxation's own -debug-only output shows the 4-byte figure (bb with just beqz: size=0x4). So loops that contain branches are overestimated by 2 bytes per branch. (b) As a result, 'Nothing that fit before became longer' / 'all differences long->setupi' is false in general. Reviewer kernel k3 (outer lp.setupi around one software and three padded hardware inner loops, rv32imc, -O2 and -Os, logs/20-F025-review/k3-pessimization): base encodes lp.setupi x1 with end offset 60, which is valid and correct. The new build takes the 12-byte long form (lp.endi +62). This happens for PRE=2 and 4 bytes, and for PRE=0/2/4 with the setup first in its block. The same holds for k2 at PRE=20 bytes (new long form where the real lp.setupi offset would be 56). This is a missed optimisation, not a miscompile, and it is acceptable, but the note and the result must describe it (and the comment at PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp:921-933 should not say 'exactly'). (c) Near 8190 the note says the bound is conservative by '<= 6 bytes'. For nested loops the reviewer measured up to about 36 bytes: k2 with an lp.setup outer loop (reg count, rv32imc) becomes a software loop from PRE=8120, where base still encodes setup1+8154..8190 correctly. k2 with a long-form outer loop becomes a software loop from 8124, where base encodes endi +8164..8188. The cause is the per-nested-setup allowance (:350) plus the branch overestimate. This is fine for real code (no SDK kernel is near 8 KB), but the note must state it.

verified_ok.encoding_limits: Correct. RISCVInstrInfoXpulp.td has LOOPxsetupi uimmS = Inst{19-15} (5 bits) and LOOPxsetup/starti/endi uimmL = Inst{31-20} (12 bits), both unsigned halfword offsets. RISCVMCCodeEmitter creates the fixup at offset 0, so the PC is the setup instruction's own address. RISCVAsmBackend checks isUInt<6>/isUInt<13> plus evenness, giving a maximum of 62 / 8190. GVSoC2 (gvsoc2/core/models/cpu/iss/include/isa/pulp_v2.hpp:903-945, isa_pulpv2.py Format_HL0/HL1): end = pc + (uimm << 1), pc = the setup's (or lp.endi's) own PC, unsigned 5- and 12-bit fields. The end address is the last instruction of the loop, and the pass labels exactly that (the LoopEnd block starts at it). So lp.setupi <= 62 is right, with no off-by-one. lp.setup <= 8190 is right. For the long form, lp.endi sits 4 bytes after the old setupi position and the body moves by 8, so the setupi-relative bound <= 8186 in removeTooLongLoops (:326ff) is right.
verified_ok.padding_model: The padding model matches emission: nops go in the setup's block, or in their own PadMBB with no alignment (the F013 layout). Only a setup that is not first in its block is moved to a new Align(4) block (runOnMachineFunction), and measureHwLoop's Known/Pad logic mirrors exactly that. A long form is not realigned and not padded, which is consistent. PseudoLOOPend has size 0, and the End label comes before it.
verified_ok.fixed_point: Terminates and is monotone. Each iteration makes exactly one change (one expansion or one padding). A setupi can be expanded only once (the long form is not isHardwareLoop). A padded loop keeps LoopLen >= 4, because nothing removes instructions. Inserting bytes can only raise alignTo results. When an inner setupi is expanded, its alignment pad (at most 2 bytes) goes away, but 8 bytes are added. So no measured quantity decreases, and there is no oscillation. An overestimate (for branches) stays an overestimate through alignTo. Nested loops: the outer loop is re-measured after every change to an inner loop.
verified_ok.removeTooLongLoops: Correct software fallback. It runs before fixupLoopLatch, and no blocks have been created yet, so MachineLoopInfo is still valid. The compare-and-branch and the counter are still present, so deleting the setup leaves a complete software loop, the same mechanism as removeUncountableLoops. The count register just becomes dead. The other hardware-loop level is not touched: an outer loop's bound includes its inner loops, so an inner loop can never be removed while its outer loop stays. Verified on GVSoC for every reviewer near-8190 case.

other_findings_not_blocking: Pre-existing, serious, affects the default clang flags: hardware loops break with linker relaxation. Without -mno-relax the assembler emits R_RISCV_ALIGN max-padding nops before the 4-byte-aligned setup blocks, and resolves the lp.setup/lp.endi PC-relative offsets at assembly time: shouldForceRelocation returns false for fixup_pulpv2_loop_*. ld.lld then deletes the nops, so the loop end addresses become wrong. Reviewer kernel k3 built by int-20 (base) without -mno-relax: in the .o, lp.endi pointed to the right instruction. After linking, 6 bytes of nops were gone and the program hung on GVSoC. With -mno-relax it is correct. Evidence: logs/20-F025-review/relax-hang/. Candidate backlog item. The worker's and the fuzzer's harnesses all pass -mno-relax, so they never see it.

Pre-existing: a loop that goes to the long form while tiny (possible only with a small -pulp-loop-range-immediate) is not padded, in base or in new. For example, with range 0, a loop of two 2-byte instructions keeps the long form with LoopLen 2.

Pre-existing: PseudoBR/Bcc/PseudoRET size overestimate in getInstSizeInBytes also affects the LoopLen<4 padding decision. A loop whose body contains a compressible branch can skip padding it needs. Same as base.
